item.title: The Angel Who Called Himself Azarias
item.description: A blind old man, a nervous young man, a bride with a very bad wedding-night record, a large fish, a dog with no name, and a travelling companion who is not quite who he says he is. The Book of Tobit, told for bedtime, with the Archangel Raphael. What's true: The events follow the Book of Tobit, which Catholic and Orthodox Christians read as part of the Old Testament. Legend: None beyond the book itself; the dog's wagging tail comes from Saint Jerome's Latin translation. Invented for this episode: Small conversations, the travellers' jokes, and the narrator's guesses about the dog and the fish are our own; nothing invented changes what happens or what it means. Feast day: Saint Raphael is honoured with the other archangels on the twenty-ninth of September in the Catholic calendar and at the Synaxis of the Archangels on the eighth of November in the Orthodox calendar.
